lessonTitle: 62. Decomposing a vector along two non-collinear vectors
lessonTitleEnglish: Decomposing a vector along two non-collinear vectors
unit: Geometry · Chapter VIII. Coordinates and vectors
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 9 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: If a and b are not collinear, any vector p can be written as p = xa + yb, and in only one way.
stages.headlineEnglish: If a and b are not collinear, any vector p can be written as p = xa + yb, and in only one way.

stages.headline: Example: in parallelogram ABCD with AB = a, AD = b and M the midpoint of BC, AM = a + ½b.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: in parallelogram ABCD with AB = a, AD = b and M the midpoint of BC, AM = a + ½b.

stages.headline: The coefficients are unique: if xa + yb = 2a + 5b then x = 2 and y = 5.
stages.headlineEnglish: The coefficients are unique: if xa + yb = 2a + 5b then x = 2 and y = 5.

stages.headline: In parallelogram ABCD, AC = x·AB + y·AD. Find x and y.
stages.headlineEnglish: In parallelogram ABCD, AC = x·AB + y·AD. Find x and y.
